proof:
Source: steps 1 and 6 of the parent-supplied proof. Notation: μ := Lebesgue measure restricted to I, ν := Lebesgue measure restricted to J, and h(t) := (d − c)⁻¹·∫_J H(t, β) dβ.
1. Lebesgue measure on ℝ × ℝ is volume.prod volume (Measure.volume_eq_prod), and (vol|I).prod (vol|J) = (vol.prod vol)|_{I×J} (Measure.prod_restrict). So H is integrable, in particular a.e.-strongly measurable, with respect to μ.prod ν. Let H̃ be strongly measurable with H = H̃ (μ.prod ν)-a.e. (AEStronglyMeasurable.mk, AEStronglyMeasurable.ae_eq_mk).
2. Let h̃(t) := (d − c)⁻¹·∫_J H̃(t, β) dβ = (d − c)⁻¹·∫ H̃(t, β) dν(β). Then h̃ is strongly measurable (StronglyMeasurable.integral_prod_right', then multiplication by a constant).
3. Apply Measure.ae_ae_of_ae_prod to H = H̃ (μ.prod ν)-a.e.: for μ-a.e. t, H(t, ·) = H̃(t, ·) ν-a.e. For such t, h(t) = h̃(t) (integral_congr_ae). Thus h = h̃ μ-a.e.
4. Rewrite the hypothesis with ae_restrict_iff' (I and J are measurable): for μ-a.e. t there is k_t with H(t, ·) = k_t ν-a.e. For such t,
   ∫_J H(t, β) dβ = ∫_J k_t dβ = (d − c)·k_t
   (integral_congr_ae, setIntegral_const, Real.volume_Ioo, using d − c > 0). Hence h(t) = k_t, and H(t, α) = h(t) for ν-a.e. α.
5. Combining steps 3 and 4: for μ-a.e. t, for ν-a.e. α, H̃(t, α) = H(t, α) = h(t) = h̃(t).
6. The set E := {p : H̃(p) = h̃(p.1)} is measurable, since H̃ and h̃∘Prod.fst are strongly measurable (StronglyMeasurable.measurableSet_eq_fun). By Measure.ae_prod_iff_ae_ae and step 5, H̃(p) = h̃(p.1) for (μ.prod ν)-a.e. p.
7. Prod.fst is quasi-measure-preserving from μ.prod ν to μ (Measure.quasiMeasurePreserving_fst, with QuasiMeasurePreserving.ae). So step 3 gives h̃(p.1) = h(p.1) for (μ.prod ν)-a.e. p.
8. By steps 1, 6 and 7, H(p) = H̃(p) = h̃(p.1) = h(p.1) for (μ.prod ν)-a.e. p. Equivalently (ae_restrict_iff' for the measurable set I × J), this holds for Lebesgue-a.e. p in I × J. This is the claim, since h(p.1) = (d − c)⁻¹·∫_J H(p.1, β) dβ. ∎
